<thought>Based on the ESI‑MS data, the most intense ion is at m/z 183.045, which corresponds to [M+H]⁺. Subtracting a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈182.0378 Da. The isotopic pattern shows a strong M+2 peak (~33 % of the base peak), characteristic of a single chlorine atom (⁴⁰Cl/³⁷Cl). Removing the mass of Cl (34.9689 Da) leaves ≈147.069 Da to be accounted for by C, H, and O. The combination C₆H₁₁O₄ matches this residual mass within a few millidaltons and gives a reasonable double‑bond equivalent. Therefore the molecular formula that fits the exact mass and isotopic pattern is C₆H₁₁O₄Cl.</thought>
<final_answer>C6H11O4Cl</final_answer>
